name: Stan Store
tagline: Mobile-first link-in-bio store for products, courses, bookings, and leads

pricing.notes: Working normalization from the official public pricing structure. Recheck the source page immediately before publication.

tiers.name: Creator
tiers.limits: Unlimited course products, storefront products, bookings, recurring subscriptions, lead magnets, community and AutoDM.

tiers.name: Creator Pro
tiers.limits: Creator features plus payment plans, discounts, limited quantity, upsells/order bumps, Afterpay/Klarna, funnels, affiliates, broadcasts and flows.

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; upgrades are prorated immediately
pricing.hiddenCosts: Stan's platform fee is 0%, but US card processing is 2.9% + $0.30; Afterpay is 6% + $0.30, Klarna 5.99% + $0.30, international cards +1.5%, currency conversion +1%, recurring billing +0.5%, and payouts 0.25% + $0.25 with a $1 minimum. Stripe fees are not refunded; Creator Pro cannot be self-downgraded during the first 30 days.

verdictSummary: Do not mistake the interface for the product. Stan Store's durable value is payments, network, compliance, which a solo one-shot build cannot reproduce responsibly. The prompt therefore builds only the closest honest personal consolation tool.
coreLoopDIY: Build a narrow creator storefront storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
diyTimeEstimate: not a true replacement; consolation build in one to two days
replacementScope: consolation build only; the paid product's moat remains
requirements: Stripe account and API keys in .env
Explicit README warning that this is a consolation build, not a production replacement
whatYouLose: tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations
whyPeopleStillPay: Stan Store: Creators pay to outsource payments, tax complexity, disputes, deliverability, moderation, and the trust needed to convert strangers.
ongoingBurden: Own payments, webhooks, refunds, tax records, fraud, access control, file delivery, moderation, backups, and support.

alternatives.name: systeme.io
alternatives.desc: Products, one course, checkout, email and bookings on a free plan; mobile-first link-page polish is not included.

rejectedAlternatives.name: CourseLit
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Products and courses fit, but bookings and the mobile link-in-bio storefront do not.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Ghost
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Membership posts are useful; bookings, product checkout and course delivery are missing.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Medusa
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It can power products after development, not a finished mobile creator store with bookings and leads.

notes: Credibility row: Stan Store survives for a structural reason, not because its interface is difficult to copy.
prompt:
Build the closest honest consolation tool inspired by Stan Store; do not claim to replace its structural moat.
Use exactly this stack: Next.js 15 + TypeScript + PostgreSQL + Stripe.
Primary job: Build a narrow creator storefront storefront or member area for one creator, using Stripe Checkout and explicit digital-delivery rules.
Start from an empty folder and create the complete working project.
Make the default mode single-user and private.
Store user data locally unless the core job requires the declared self-hosted database.
Do not add analytics, telemetry, ads, or third-party accounts.
Put every secret and external credential in .env and provide .env.example.
Use realistic sample data that is clearly labelled and easy to delete.
Implement the smallest polished interface that completes the core loop end to end.
Include clear empty, loading, validation, success, and failure states.
Add import and export so the user is not trapped in the app.
Use accessible keyboard navigation, labels, focus states, and sensible contrast.
Validate untrusted input and never log secrets or private file contents.
Deliberately exclude these paid-product advantages: marketplace discovery and buyer trust; tax, disputes, payouts, and fraud operations; native apps and community moderation.
Do not fake integrations, network effects, proprietary data, model quality, compliance, or security claims.
Where an external API is optional, keep the app useful without it and explain the degraded mode.
Write focused unit tests for the data model and the most important workflow.
Add one end-to-end smoke test that proves the core loop works.
Create a README with setup, permissions, architecture, data location, backup, and limitations.
Add scripts for install, development, test, build, and a production-style local run.
Run the tests and build before finishing, then fix errors rather than merely describing them.
